evidence.quote: The results of this examination were not at first very enlightening, though our tabulation of them seemed to reveal a fairly significant trend; namely, that the number of reported horrors was by far the greatest in areas either comparatively near the avoided house or connected with it by stretches of the morbidly overnourished forest.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator and his colleague systematically tabulate reported incidents and detect a geographic trend correlating horrors with proximity to the mansion.

evidence.quote: We did, however, deem ourselves justified in assuming that it was a living organism highly susceptible to electrical storms; and although certain of the stories suggested wings, we believed that its aversion for open spaces made land locomotion a more probable theory.
evidence.paraphrase: The investigators reason from conflicting accounts to form hypotheses about the creature's nature and mode of movement.

evidence.quote: Simple animals they were, gently descending the evolutionary scale because of their unfortunate ancestry and stultifying isolation.
evidence.paraphrase: The squatters are explained as having degenerated along an evolutionary trajectory due to ancestry and isolation.

evidence.quote: Of a possible seventy-five natives who had inhabited this spot, not one living specimen was visible. The disordered earth was covered with blood and human debris bespeaking too vividly the ravages of demon teeth and talons; yet no visible trail led away from the carnage.
evidence.paraphrase: An entire village of about seventy-five people is wiped out in a single night, leaving mangled corpses.

evidence.quote: It was the ultimate product of mammalian degeneration; the frightful outcome of isolated spawning, multiplication, and cannibal nutrition above and below the ground; the embodiment of all the snarling chaos and grinning fear that lurk behind life.
evidence.paraphrase: The creatures are explained as the product of biological degeneration from isolated inbreeding and cannibalism.

evidence.quote: One eye was blue, the other brown. They were the dissimilar Martense eyes of the old legends, and I knew in one inundating cataclysm of voiceless horror what had become of that vanished family; the terrible and thunder-crazed house of Martense.
evidence.paraphrase: The heterochromatic eyes reveal the creatures are the degenerated descendants of the Martense family.

evidence.quote: In appearance all were marked by a peculiar inherited dissimilarity of eyes; one generally being blue and the other brown.
evidence.paraphrase: The Martense family carries an inherited trait of mismatched eye colors across generations.

evidence.quote: Their social contacts grew fewer and fewer, till at last they took to intermarrying with the numerous menial class about the estate. Many of the crowded family degenerated, moved across the valley, and merged with the mongrel population which was later to produce the pitiful squatters.
evidence.paraphrase: Generations of isolation and intermarriage lead the family to degenerate and diverge into the squatter population.

evidence.quote: Presently, as I gazed abstractedly at the moonlit panorama, my eye became attracted by something singular in the nature and arrangement of a certain topographical element.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator observes and analyzes the spatial arrangement of the mounds to deduce a pattern.

evidence.quote: That summit was undeniably a center from which the lines or rows of points radiated indefinitely and irregularly, as if the unwholesome Martense mansion had thrown out visible tentacles of terror.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator deduces that the mounds radiate outward from the mansion as an underground tunnel network.

evidence.quote: That I am still alive and sane, is a marvel I can not fathom.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator expresses astonishment at his own survival and sanity after seeing the shadow.

evidence.quote: I can not sleep at night now, and have to take opiates when it thunders.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator describes lasting trauma requiring opiates during thunderstorms.

evidence.quote: I had recovered enough in a week to send to Albany for a gang of men to blow up the Martense mansion and the entire top of Tempest Mountain with dynamite, stop up all the discoverable mound-burrows, and destroy certain overnourished trees whose very existence seemed an insult to sanity.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator arranges to dynamite the mansion and mountain top and seal the burrows.

evidence.quote: Who can, with my knowledge, think of the earth's unknown caverns without a nightmare dread of future possibilities?
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator suggests his discovery casts dread over the reader's ordinary sense of the wider world.

evidence.quote: The thing will haunt me, for who can say the extermination is complete, and that analogous phenomena do not exist all over the world?
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator extrapolates that similar hidden degenerate phenomena may exist worldwide.

evidence.quote: we deem ourselves justified in assuming that it was a living organism highly susceptible to electrical storms
evidence.paraphrase: The creature is characterized as an organism whose activity is triggered by electrical storms.

evidence.quote: a burst of multitudinous and leprous life\u2014a loathsome night-spawned flood of organic corruption more devastatingly hideous than the blackest conjurations of mortal madness and morbidity.
evidence.paraphrase: A swarm of thousands of creatures pours out of the ground to spread death across the region.

evidence.quote: Would to God I had let them share the search, that I might not have had to bear the secret alone so long; to bear it alone for fear the world would call me mad or go mad itself at the demon implications of the thing.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator laments bearing the secret alone out of fear others would think him mad.
